_comment: Worker safety settings (passed to every worker by start-worker.sh --safety). Replace /ABSOLUTE/PATH with the absolute path of the project's core copy, <project>/coordinator/core (the folder that holds scripts/). This is the SWARM and STANDARD baseline (CORE section 3): only the protected branches and irreversible removals are guarded; workers do routine risky work themselves and report it. The STRICT preset adds "Bash(gh pr merge*)", "Bash(gh pr ready*)" and the production MCP write tools; the CAUTIOUS override also adds "Read(**/.env*)" and the stack candidates chosen in the init quiz (TOOLKIT.md Safety). Also add gh pr merge / ready denies wherever PROJECT.md says humans merge or mark ready. MCP tools bypass the hook (it sees only the shell and edit tools), so their writes are denied here: the names assume the GitHub MCP server is connected as "github" (mcp__<server>__<tool>) - rename them to the server name this machine uses, and add the write tools of any other connected server that can change a protected branch. Drop mcp__github__merge_pull_request only where workers merge their own PRs (PROJECT.md). attribution hides the AI co-author trailer, the PR line and the session link: artifacts are in the owner's voice (CORE section 11). env COORD_PROTECTED_ROOT is the project's working copy (the owner's checkout, the project root): replace /ABSOLUTE/PROJECT with its absolute path - a project of several repositories lists every repository's root there, separated by | (/ABSOLUTE/BACKEND|/ABSOLUTE/FRONTEND), each protected alike; an entry that is empty, not absolute or not a folder on this machine makes the guard refuse every edit tool's call, naming it (TOOLKIT.md Safety); the guard then refuses Edit / Write / MultiEdit / NotebookEdit under it outside its .claude/worktrees/ (hence those tools in the PreToolUse matcher). env COORD_PROTECTED_BRANCHES names the branches the guard protects besides main and master, which it always protects (empty here: main and master only): names separated by spaces or commas, each matched whole and literally (no patterns), letter case ignored - a list adds to main and master, never replaces them; the push deny rules below name main and master only - a project listing more branches adds the same deny rules for each of them (TOOLKIT.md Safety). SendMessage is in the matcher too: the guard refuses a message to a session of another project, as it refuses claude stop / rm / respawn / attach / --resume of one (CORE section 1.17). Start load (#603): a worker runs in the background and its questions go to the coordinator, so four keys keep what it never uses out of every request (measured on Windows: a start of 60k tokens down to 39k): enableArtifact false drops the Artifact tool (publishing a page on claude.ai; a worker reports by SendMessage and writes files); the five bare tool names in permissions.deny - AskUserQuestion, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, SendFeedback, Workflow - drop those tools (no person is there to ask, the code-review skill's typed output, self-paced loops and a fallback wake-up beside a background wait, feedback drafts, multi-agent workflows): a bare name takes the tool out of the session, it guards nothing; syncClaudeAiSkills false stops loading the skills synced from claude.ai (in this session only: from a file passed with --settings nothing is moved or deleted); skillOverrides turns off every coord-* skill the core ships, each of which says Coordinator only - a project turns off its own coordinator-only skills the same way (a plugin's skills do not follow this key). MCP servers and plugins stay as they are: no key here touches them. This file only - never the coordinator's own settings, which edit there (TOOLKIT.md Safety).
